title: When attachment keeps binding the mind
issueStatement: The heart feels dragged around by approval, comfort, possession, or a version of life you do not want to lose.
centralInsight: Attachment is not only affection. In Gurbani it is the mind becoming bound to what cannot hold the weight you place on it.
practicalReflection: Attachment is revealed by the force of your reactions: what you cannot imagine losing without collapse often owns more of you than you realize.
actionPrompt: Name the thing whose fluctuation keeps deciding your inner state. Bring that honestly into prayer.

source.shortMeaning: Pleasure can become the very place where desire for God thins out.
source.lifeApplication: Attachment often hides inside the comfort you least want disturbed.

excerpts.explanation: Guru Nanak links attachment to the sedating power of unchecked comfort.

source.shortMeaning: Greed, attachment, praise, and blame lose their grip in steadiness.
source.lifeApplication: Freedom is pictured as not being constantly touched by these hooks.

excerpts.explanation: This shabad describes what the unhooked heart looks like.

source.shortMeaning: Mercy and Naam loosen the heart's dependence on lesser securities.
source.lifeApplication: Attachment weakens when life is received as gift, not possession.

excerpts.explanation: The movement from mercy to Naam offers a healthier center of trust.
